name: IDFC First Bank
description: IDFC First Bank is a relatively young private sector bank that was formed from the merger of IDFC Bank and Capital First in 2018. Under CEO V. Vaidyanathan, the bank has transformed from an infrastructure-focused wholesale lender into a retail-focused franchise, growing its retail deposit base from near zero to over ₹1.8 lakh crore. It is now building a full-service consumer banking proposition with mobile-first products.
verdict_reason: High optionality from retail transformation but credit quality uncertainty in current macro remains a blocking concern
verdict_memo: IDFC First Bank is a genuine transformation story — V. Vaidyanathan's execution in building a retail franchise from scratch is remarkable, and the deposit franchise is now sticky and low-cost. The blocking concern is asset quality: the bank has significant legacy infrastructure loans and is building out into retail lending in a segment that is showing early signs of stress across the industry. If asset quality holds through the current cycle and the bank demonstrates sustainable ROE > 12%, it moves to shortlisted. Watch Q2 FY27 GNPA trend closely.

laxmi.notes: Bank-specific metrics: CASA ratio at 48% (exceptional for a bank of this vintage). NIM 6.1% — strong. GNPA 2.2% (managed). ROE 9% — still below cost of equity but improving. Capital adequacy 16.2% — well-capitalised. No pledging by promoters. Auditor BSR & Co (KPMG affiliate) — stable.

meera.notes: Stock 45% below 3-year high — clear underperformance relative to banking peers. Nifty Bank has recovered but IDFC First has lagged. Delivery % 65% — moderate. No promoter open-market buying. Pattern suggests institutional patience, not accumulation.

tara.notes: V. Vaidyanathan is one of the most credible banking executives in India — built Capital First from scratch and delivered on every milestone. Consistent narrative: retail transformation, low-cost deposits, branch expansion. Moat is the low-cost retail deposit franchise once established — difficult to replicate. Key risk is execution quality in consumer lending as competition intensifies.
tara.guidance_track_record: sets multi-year targets and hits them; transparent about credit cost cycles
tara.key_risk: Consumer credit stress (MFI, personal loans) in FY26-27 could spike credit costs and delay ROE improvement

optionality.worst_case: Credit costs spike to 3%+ in FY27; ROE stays below 10% for 2 more years; stock remains range-bound at current levels. Bank remains solvent and growing — downside is time, not capital loss.
optionality.best_case_optionality: ROE crosses 15% by FY28; deposit franchise re-rates from 1× to 2× book value; stock doubles from current levels as the market recognises a fully-formed retail bank franchise.
optionality.archetype: Kotak Mahindra Bank 2010 — when the retail transformation was underway but profitability metrics hadn't yet caught up; Kotak 8×'d as ROE improved over the following decade
